title: Nintendo: The Console Wars
summary: By the midpoint of the 8-bit generation in the NES, it looks like Nintendo's moat is impenetrable. That's what was so game-changing about EA's John Madden Football. They're right in the middle of these negotiations with Sega because Trip and EA had famously gone out and reverse engineered the Genesis in a cleanroom.

thesis: This episode argues that Nintendo's historical defensive strategy and lack of focus on backwards compatibility created a massive opening for competitors like Sega and Sony, who eventually dominated the market. However, the Switch represents a perfect strategic comeback by targeting underserved mid-core and indie markets with high monetization potential, proving that Nintendo can win again despite having the deck stacked against them.

claims.quote: If Nintendo had just been aggressive and obsoleted themselves, they would have probably been in a great position. But instead, they sat back, they tried to play defense, they tried to give enough running room to their NES to keep making good money as long as possible, then it left this opening for Sega to come in and pull this move, and then suddenly, Nintendo no longer has an advantage to leverag

claims.claim: Nintendo didn't know the importance of backwards compatibility today, which becomes a huge mistake.
claims.quote: You couldn't do that back in the day, but this is so important to feathering in each new console generation that literally billions of dollars of engineering across, not only hardware, but software titles are invested in this today. Nintendo didn't know that, but this becomes a huge, huge mistake. That's one.

claims.claim: EA's John Madden Football was game-changing because it simulated the game of football in a way nothing coming out of Japan could.
claims.quote: That's what was so game-changing about EA's John Madden Football. It was 11 on 11, real football with real playbooks. If you ever played football, if you were a student of the game, or if you watch the NFL every Sunday, it was still a rudimentary video game by today's standards, but this was actually simulating the game of football in a way that nothing coming out of Japan really ever could.
